# Bounded WINDOW rendering attribution

WINDOW-STANDING-DELIVERY-20260910-R1 authorizes up to three additional diagnostic campaigns, counted at dispatch in the task ledger. This first campaign reuses the reviewed A/B experiment after a host-policy correction; it is not required acceptance CI. Both diagnostic sources descend from8dccb85 (candidate d5 plus the existing exact six-line success-retention hook). A adds only the shared observer and console bridge. B has identical observation bytes and only generated-window glass transmission0.5→0. The B intervention must never be shipped as a production fix merely because it passes.

`sources.json` binds A/B commit/tree/parent/foundation. `source-variants.mjs` verifies sole-parent ancestry, the original retained hook, exact reviewed observation-file hashes, unchanged lockfile and an exact one-literal pair delta. Precommit preparation pins are deliberately not runnable; full immutable pins must be filled and physically verified after independent review before publication. The harness commit is neither application variant. Only the existing diagnostic ref/manual registered workflow243196740 is used; no product PR/ref changes.

The source observer installs through existing design-canvas onCreated, before its first renderer call according to the locked R3F implementation. It wraps `render`, `renderBufferDirect`, and `setRenderTarget`, forwarding original this/arguments/returns/exceptions. Actual generated glass is selected by existing `generated-window-glass-3d` object metadata plus physical-material type. Numeric object/material/renderer/target IDs, current transmission/side, target dimensions, calls, draw-counter deltas and JS durations are recorded. Other positive-transmission materials are observed, not mutated. Actual Three draw functions update the renderer info counter after WebGL draw dispatch; reaching renderBufferDirect alone is not counted as a demonstrated draw. These observations are not GPU execution times or direct named-private-pass instrumentation.

The record is capped at2048 ordinary events plus one limit event per document module instance. Up to64 material descriptors per renderer are remembered. Repeated calls continue normally after the record cap. The limit event's omission count is explicitly a lower bound; later omissions cannot be reconstructed without another retained snapshot. A cap/error during A causes the B admission check to reject. Renderer begin, target begin and first generated direct entry records precede their corresponding call. Recording uses no new timer/frame/invalidation, screenshots, readback, GPU wait, priority changes or native tooling. Observer elapsed time includes measured synchronous capture/serialization/log-enqueue work through the prior event, not asynchronous transport cost; later overhead after a cap is unavailable.

The existing console callback passes only fixed-schema numeric/enum observations, explicit per-document browser time origins, and host-side reload/admission markers. Malformed observations become safe observer-error markers without changing fatalErrors, assertions, runtime outcomes or deadlines. Clock markers precede the unchanged heartbeat in each document, so render and heartbeat performance.now timestamps share a document origin. Host receipt sequence establishes message order, not an invented zero-latency clock alignment. B's separate admission check requires installed observation, one clock, started heartbeat, reload1 and its admission-start marker, and a completed positive-transmission generated draw paired with earlier render/material entry in that same document. It does not claim exact GPU/admission overlap. Exact original A cleanup remains a separate mandatory gate. No useful target capture means B is NOT EXECUTED.

All existing source/auth, child-environment, package, strict-artifact, runtime and resource owners are reused. The only resource-name validation adaptation is C/T→A/B for the synthetic bootstrap names. No lifecycle or cleanup check is weakened. Candidate A/B use the candidate lifecycle; the historical T receipt remains unavailable. A failure stays a failure even if B runs and passes. The original two cases, furniture, three reloads,42s admission/10s evaluation, one worker/zero retries, browser arguments/backend and all preconditions remain.

One standard Ubuntu24.04 runner,120min, A then conditionally B, at most two strict builds/two complete runtimes. Only the exact pairs (Ubuntu24.04.4 LTS,image20260831.293.1) and (Ubuntu24.04.5 LTS,image20260907.300.1) are accepted; cross-pairs and unknown/missing values reject. Runner2.337.0, Node24.13.0, Chromium148.0.7778.96/rev1223 checks stay unchanged. A/B have separate clone/dependencies/artifacts/auth/PostgreSQL15 bootstrap and Stable resources. No automatic host-list update is allowed. Justified successors may run within the standing phase ceiling. Both variants share the actual allocated host; cross-campaign timings are not a controlled comparison.

The campaign command is `node .github/diagnostics/window-linux/campaign.mjs`. It retains the working original prerequisites and `npm run evidence:production:build`, then `runtime-worker.mjs` calling the unchanged Stable owner. One private root `$RUNNER_TEMP/window-linux-standing-r1-01`, A/B output directories, one allowlisted sanitized artifact max100MiB/seven days. Raw command logs/auth/DOM/context/protocol remain private and are not uploaded. Exact-owned normal cleanup and container service binding remain mandatory; no forced DROP, session termination or renewed deadline. Preflight mismatch stops before builds/runtimes.

Local focused checks in the task-owned layout with sibling `a-source`/`b-source`: `node --test .github/diagnostics/window-linux/host-policy.test.mjs .github/diagnostics/window-linux/focused.test.mjs .github/diagnostics/window-linux/render-observation.test.mjs`. They exercise actual observer modules, actual generated React material properties and locked Three object types with explicit in-memory renderer/lifecycle stand-ins, plus exact staged source trees; they are not browser/GPU/DB/build evidence. Existing host/auth/retention tests are reused with A/B bindings. After commits, run actual source and pair verifiers again before the sole publication. The independent review must assess observation sufficiency, observer-induced-delay risk, privacy and strict-owner compatibility before any commit/publication.

Interpretation remains diagnostic. Compare actual material draws, target/frame timings, heartbeat/admission behavior and independent original test outcomes. Same-run order/cache, compilation/loading, other transmissive materials, observer overhead and missing GPU/native attribution remain confounders. A B-only pass does not clear CI or establish cause. No production downgrade, required-candidate campaign, HTTPS GateA3, deployment or canonical integration is authorized.
